title: What is known about 1RB---_0RC0LD_1LB1RC_0LE0LF_1RD1LE_1RF1RA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB---_0RC0LD_1LB1RC_0LE0LF_1RD1LE_1RF1RA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state machine halts from blank tape. The tape is almost all 1s: blocks separated by single 0s, plus one double 0 near the left end. At the left end a zigzag cuts the first block down to two thirds of its length, over and over, a little like writing a number in base 3/2; at the right end the machine merges blocks back together.
verdict: The question is open, but it is now an exact question about one pattern. Lean proves (kernel only) that the machine is a rewriting system on lists of block lengths, the block map, and that it halts from blank tape if and only if the block map reaches the frame 0 1 1 C>0 1. The other two critical frames, 0 1 B>1 1 1 and F>1 1, are excluded by an invariant. That frame can only be reached in a sweep of the head to the right, and whether a sweep halts is read off the block list where it starts. By native_decide none of the first 108 frames is critical (3.0·1011 machine steps). Whether a halting sweep ever starts is not known.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (A1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 3,612 cells have been visited and 3,609 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: No halt in the first 2.75·10<sup>23</sup> steps (accelerated run)
claims.text: tools/c/rleaccel.cpp, the compiled port of the run-length simulator tools/py/bbtools/rleaccel.py (same rules: blocks of 1 cell, runs crossed in one step, cycle jumps only after their one-cycle rule is proved symbolically; tested against the Python program by tools/tests/test_rleaccel_cpp.py), runs from blank tape without a halt to 2.75·1023 machine steps (exact count; tape spanning 237,881,298 cells). It ran about 30 minutes and was resumed from a checkpoint after interruptions, so its macro-step count (9,160,000,000) is not that of an uninterrupted run; the step count it reports is exact either way.

claims.title: The block map
claims.text: Write the tape as blocks of 1s, each followed by one 0 (a block may be empty, so 0 0 is an empty block). A frame is a state E, C, B or F and the lists of block lengths left and right of the head. The map next (16 cases, each a formula on the first one or two block lengths of each side) sends every frame to the next frame the machine reaches; this is proved for all block lists, each case by one symbolic run.

claims.title: It halts iff the block map reaches a critical frame
claims.text: The block map is undefined exactly at three kinds of frames: C just after a block of exactly two 1s when the cell after the next is a 1 (0 1 1 C>0 1); B on a block of at least three 1s just after a block of exactly one 1 (0 1 B>1 1 1); F on a block of at least two 1s (F>1 1). From each the machine halts within 8 steps. The run from blank tape reaches the frame B [1] [] after one step, and the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the orbit of that frame under the block map reaches a critical frame.

claims.title: No critical frame among the first 10<sup>8</sup> frames
claims.text: The block map is defined 10<sup>8</sup> times in a row from the first frame, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: An invariant of every frame: two of the three critical frames are never reached
claims.text: After the first frame, every E frame is E L (m :: 0 :: R') with m ≥ 1 and no other empty block (the tape blk(L) E>0 1^m 0 0 blk(R') has exactly one double 0); every C frame has at least two blocks on its left, the second not empty, and an empty block on its right only first; every B frame has at least five 1s left of the head and no empty block; and no F frame is ever reached. So the critical frames 0 1 B>1 1 1 and F>1 1 never occur, and the machine halts iff the block map reaches C (2 :: L) (r+1 :: R), never straight from an E frame.

claims.title: It halts iff some sweep to the right starts on a bad block list
claims.text: While the head moves right through C frames, each step moves one block from the right list to the left list, until the first block of 0 or 1 cells: a 0 turns the head round, a 1 halts unless it is the last block. A sweep starts at a B frame (or at E L (1 :: 0 :: R)). The machine halts from blank tape iff the run reaches a sweep start whose right list r₀, r₁, … has r₀ = 3 and r₁ ≥ 1, or r₀ ≠ 2 and a block of exactly one 1, not the last, before the first block of 0.

claims.title: A descent at the left end that ends after an even cut starts its sweep on 4u+1 cells
claims.text: E [] (18u+6 :: 0 :: j :: R) reaches B [8u+7] (4u+1 :: j+6u+1 :: R) in 30u + 7 frames. After the first cut every value of a left-end descent is even, so a descent whose last cut is from a block divisible by 3 hands the sweep a first block of 1, 5, 9, 13, … cells, never 3. A first block of 3 needs the odd block of 15 of halts_of_15.

claims.title: 10<sup>8</sup> frames are 300,362,311,724 steps
claims.text: The same map in Python, with the step count of each case, reaches 300,362,311,724 machine steps after 10<sup>8</sup> frames (at most 16 blocks on the tape). Compared with the machine itself step by step for the first 3,000,000 steps: 42,875 frames, each reached at exactly the step the map says.

claims.title: The splitting step
claims.text: Each time the head is at the left end in state E on a 0, the tape starts E>0 1^x 0 0 1^y …. In the first 109 steps, 810 of the 1,241 consecutive pairs of such moments are a splitting step: the next one is E>0 1^x' 0 0 1^y' … with x' = ⌈2x/3⌉ and y' = y + (x − x') + 1 (the new second block sometimes written 1 0 1^(y'−2)), the rest of the tape unchanged. The others come after a pass at the right end.

claims.title: Cost of a split
claims.text: A splitting step from a block of x cells takes about x²/3 steps (2,827,525 steps for x = 2,903; 84,477 for x = 494).

claims.title: Growth shape: power/power
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.328). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.345).

claims.title: How the cut is made
claims.text: In the block map the cut is three cases in a row: E (i :: L) (m :: 0 :: j :: R) goes to C (m−2 :: i+2 :: L) (0 :: j :: R), to C (1 :: m−3 :: i+2 :: L) (j :: R) and to E (i+2 :: L) (m−3 :: 0 :: j+1 :: R) (for m ≥ 5): the block left of the head gains 2 cells, the block being cut loses 3, the block behind the double 0 gains 1. Each of the three cases is proved, and so is their composition over a whole cut (zig, below).

claims.title: A whole zigzag in one rule
claims.text: From E (i :: L) (m+2+3t :: 0 :: j :: R) the block map reaches E (i+2t :: L) (m+2 :: 0 :: j+t :: R) after 3t frames, for every t: the block being cut loses 3t cells, the block on its left gains 2t, the block behind the double 0 gains t. At the left end of the tape the first trip is special (zig1_end).

claims.title: Cutting a block of exactly 15 cells at the left end halts
claims.text: If the run from blank tape ever reaches E [] (15 :: 0 :: j :: R), the machine halts: 23 frames later the frame is critical. The same happens away from the left end for a block of 9 with 4 cells on its left, 12 with 2, and 6 with 6 (critical_mid, stated for the block map from those frames). None of these frames has been seen in the run.

claims.title: Cutting a block of exactly 2 or 3 cells at the left end never halts
claims.text: From E [] (2 :: 0 :: j :: R) two frames lead to E [] (2 :: 0 :: j+1 :: R), forever; a block of 3 becomes a block of 2 in two frames. So if the run from blank tape ever reaches one of these frames, the machine does not halt. Neither frame has been seen in the run.

claims.title: No critical frame until the tape holds 5.3·10<sup>10</sup> ones
claims.text: A C program runs the block map with every zigzag taken in one step (the rule above) and tests each frame for the three critical frames and for the left-end loop. From the first frame it runs 249,644,974,080 such steps without either; the tape then holds 53,495,934,532 ones. It gives the same frame as py/blockmap.py after the first 4·107 frames of the block map. The program counts its own steps, not machine steps; the earlier accelerated run reached 5.3·107 cells at 3.08·1021 machine steps, and steps grow roughly like the cube of the width, so this is of the order of 1030 machine steps (an estimate, not a count).

claims.title: Observed: how the left end is cut
claims.text: At the left end a block of m cells is cut to 2(m+1)/3 or 2m/3 cells, again and again, until m ≡ 1 mod 3, when the head leaves to the right. After the first cut the values are even, so 15 can only be the first value of such a descent. In 6·10<sup>10</sup> steps of the C program (1.3·10<sup>10</sup> ones) descents reach a block of at most 20 cells about five times per doubling of the tape, with no sign of dying out: the values cut were 4, 6, …, 20 (15 to 25 times each) and 7, 9, 19 once each, early in the run. In 2,000 restarts from the tape at 647,185 ones with every block of 100 cells or more changed by a random 0 to 99 cells, each run until the tape had grown fourfold, none reached a critical frame or the loop; random small tapes halt often. This suggests the non-halting is structural, but no invariant is known.

claims.title: The sweep starts of the run
claims.text: In 10<sup>9</sup> frames of the block map with zigzags in one step (71,452,928 B frames, 2.1·10<sup>8</sup> ones at the end) no sweep start is bad. The first block of a sweep start, when it is not the last block, is below 32 only 140 times. The values are 1, 5, 8, 9, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 21, 25, 28, 29, 30, 31, mostly 1 mod 4, and never 2, 3, 4, 6 or 7. The smallest later block a sweep reads before turning, away from the last block, is 2 once and otherwise at least 4.

claims.title: No finite pattern invariant of the two ends closes
claims.text: After the first 10<sup>5</sup> frames, blocks below 20 cells occur only among the leftmost five or six blocks, as the last block, or next to the head. An abstract block map that keeps up to 8 blocks at each end exactly, values below T exactly and larger ones as "at least k", started from the real frame 10<sup>8</sup>, still reaches the critical frame. Each path it finds makes the last block small and then several small blocks next to each other, which the real run has not produced. What keeps the blocks large is their size, which such a model cannot hold.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. It halts iff some sweep to the right starts on a bad block list (in particular iff the block map reaches 0 1 1 C>0 1; the other two critical frames are excluded). Two exact events are known that would settle it: cutting a block of exactly 15 cells at the left end (halts) and cutting a block of exactly 2 or 3 cells there (never halts). Neither has happened while the tape grew to 5.3·1010 ones. The arithmetic of the left-end descents keeps 3 away from the first block of the sweeps they start, but blocks elsewhere are kept large only by their size, and no invariant is known that excludes the bad sweep starts. The community tracker lists the machine as a "lottery".

check: python3 holdouts/1RB---_0RC0LD_1LB1RC_0LE0LF_1RD1LE_1RF1RA/py/absint.py 30 8 8 START    # START: a frame in three lines; prints an abstract path to the critical frame
g++ -O2 -o rleaccel tools/c/rleaccel.cpp && timeout 1800 ./rleaccel 1RB---_0RC0LD_1LB1RC_0LE0LF_1RD1LE_1RF1RA 1 1000000000000000 run.ck 300    # 30 minutes

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The tape is blocks of 1s separated by 0s, and the machine moves cells from block to block: a zigzag cuts a block to two thirds, a sweep shifts every 0 one cell left. Lean proves that this block arithmetic is all the machine does, and that it halts exactly if one of three small patterns ever turns up.

facts.text: Critical frame left: the machine halts iff the block map reaches 0 1 1 C>0 1; an invariant excludes the other two.
Frames of the block map checked, none critical (3.0·10<sup>11</sup> steps).
Width after t steps (fitted exponents 0.33 and 0.35).

sections.heading: Cutting a block to two thirds
html: Stop the machine each time the head is at the left end in state E. The tape is then a few long blocks of 1s, separated by single 0s, except that the first two blocks are separated by a double 0: at step 968,072,934 it is E>0 1^494 0 0 1^248 0 1^2831.

The next three such moments are E>0 1^330 0 0 1^413 0 1^2831, E>0 1^220 0 0 1 0 1^522 0 1^2831, and then, after a pass to the right end, a long first block again. Each time the first block went to two thirds of its length, rounded up (494 → 330 → 220), and the cells it lost (plus one) went to the block after the double 0. That rule, x → ⌈2x/3⌉, held in all 810 such steps of the first 109.

The cut is made by a zigzag. Between the single 0 inside the first block and the double 0, the head goes back and forth; each trip moves the single 0 two cells right, takes three cells from the stretch between them and gives one to the block beyond the double 0. A cut of a block of x cells takes about x/3 trips of length about x, so about x²/3 steps.

sections.heading: Merging at the right end
html: When the first block gets short, the head runs to the right end in state C and works on the last blocks: at step 968,216,616 the tape ends 0 1^522 0 1^2831 0 1 C>0, and by step 972,860,864 it ends 0 1^1682 0 1^1745 0 1 C>0. Long blocks are rebuilt there, and the next left-end visit starts a new run of cuts from a long first block (2,049 cells at step 976,608,441).
The machine halts only if D reads a 1 that has a 0 on its left and two 1s on its right; the zigzag always keeps 1s on D's left, so far.

sections.heading: The machine as arithmetic on a list of blocks
html: Read the tape as blocks of 1s, each followed by one 0: 1^7 0 1^5 0 0 1^4 0 is the list 7, 5, 0, 4 (the double 0 is an empty block). Stop the machine only at four kinds of moments: E or C standing on a 0 between two blocks, B or F standing on the first cell of a block. Then the whole tape is two lists of numbers, the blocks left of the head (nearest first) and the blocks right of it.

From such a moment the machine always reaches another one, and the new lists are given by a short formula on the first one or two numbers of each list. For example, with E on a 0, i ones on its left and a block of m ≥ 2 ones on its right, the machine moves two cells of that block to the left block and stands in state C at the end of what remains: 1^i E>0 1^m 0 becomes 1^(i+2) 0 1^(m−2) C>0. With C after a block of a ≥ 3 ones, the 0 under the head moves one cell left and C runs on over the next block: 1^a C>0 1^r 0 becomes 1^(a−1) 0 1^(r+1) C>0. With C after a block of exactly one 1, the machine turns round and E runs back to the previous 0. There are 16 such cases. Lean proves each one for all block lengths and all surroundings (next_sound).

Three situations have no next frame: 0 1 1 C>0 1 (C after a block of exactly two 1s, and a 1 two cells ahead), 0 1 B>1 1 1 and F>1 1. In each the machine halts within 8 steps, and these are the only ways it can halt: Lean proves that the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the block map, started from the frame after the first step, ever reaches one of these three (halts_iff_critical). The first 108 frames, 3.0·1011 steps, do not.

The cut of the section above is three of the cases in a row; a sweep to the right is the second example repeated. Two of the three patterns are excluded for good by an invariant (next section); whether the third is ever reached is the open part.

sections.heading: Where it could halt: only at the start of a sweep
html: Lean now proves an invariant of every frame after the first (lean/Invariant.lean, kernel only). In E frames the tape has exactly one double 0, and it sits right after the block next to the head: blk(L) E>0 1^m 0 0 blk(R'), with m ≥ 1 and no other empty block. In B frames the block left of the head has at least five 1s, and there is no empty block anywhere. No F frame is ever reached. Two of the three critical frames, 0 1 B>1 1 1 and F>1 1, are therefore impossible. The machine halts iff the block map reaches 0 1 1 C>0 1 (halts_iff_C), and it can never get there straight from an E frame (critical_after_BC).

The head reaches that frame only while it moves right through C frames, in a sweep. Each step of a sweep moves one block from the right list to the left list unchanged. The sweep stops at the first block of fewer than two 1s: a 0 turns the head round, and a 1 halts the machine unless it is the last block. A sweep starts at a B frame (or, once early in the run, at E L (1 :: 0 :: R)). lean/Sweep.lean proves that the machine halts iff some sweep start has a right list r₀, r₁, r₂, … with r₀ = 3 and r₁ ≥ 1, or with r₀ ≠ 2 and a block of exactly one 1, not the last block, before the first block of 0 (halts_iff_sweep).

At the left end the descent of cuts makes every value after the first one even. lean/Cuts.lean (cut_even) computes how such a descent ends when its last two blocks are 18u + 6 and then 12u + 4: at B [8u+7] (4u+1 :: …). The sweep then starts on 1, 5, 9, 13, … cells, never 3. A start on 3 needs an odd block of 15 at the beginning of a descent, which is the halts_of_15 event. Run the block map below and look at the first block of every sweep start. The small values cluster at 1 mod 4, and 2, 3, 4, 6 and 7 never occur.

Why no simple invariant closes the question: after the first 105 frames, blocks of fewer than 20 cells occur only among the leftmost five or six blocks, as the last block, or next to the head. Every other block is larger, and most have thousands of cells or more. The right end, though, sometimes shrinks its last block to about a third. An abstract model that keeps the small blocks at both ends exactly and lumps the others into "at least N" still reaches the critical frame (py/absint.py). Each path it finds needs several small blocks in a row next to each other, which the real run has not produced. Whether the run ever produces them is the lottery the community tracker describes.

sections.heading: Why the width grows like t<sup>1/3</sup>
html: A cut costs the square of the block length over three, and a whole series of cuts (lengths x, 2x/3, 4x/9, …) costs about x²/3 · 1/(1 − 4/9) = 0.6·x² steps, of the order of the width squared, while the tape grows by only a few cells per series. That gives width3 ~ steps: 3,612 cells after 109 steps.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.328). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.345).
After 109 steps the tape spans 3,612 cells (1,026 left of the start, 1,905 right), with a density of 1s of 0.999.

The tape (run-length coded, 1^5 is five 1s, C>0 the head in state C on a 0) at some of the last moments the head reached a new cell, cut to 400 characters:

summary: Solid blocks of 1s separated by 0s; Lean proves the machine is an explicit map on lists of block lengths and halts iff it reaches 0 1 1 C>0 1 (an invariant excludes the other two critical frames), which only happens in a rightward sweep that starts on a bad block list; none among the first 10^8 frames. Also proved: cutting a block of exactly 15 cells at the left end halts, of exactly 2 or 3 never halts; neither seen while the tape grew to 5.3·10^10 ones.
